claims.text: The protective-oxide behavior of CrFeCoNiX alloys is primarily governed by the effect of X on cation diffusion kinetics and oxide/alloy interfacial energies.
Al additions slow oxidation kinetics in CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Si additions slow oxidation kinetics in CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Al promotes adherent composite scales containing Cr2O3 and (Cr,Al)2O3 by lowering interfacial energies and reducing cation mobility.
Si promotes adherent composite scales containing Cr2O3 and SiO2 interlayers by lowering interfacial energies and reducing cation mobility.
Mn promotes rapid diffusion and the formation of incompatible manganese oxides.
Mn-rich oxides generate internal or interfacial stresses that initiate cracking and spallation.
The composition, coherence, and adhesion of the mixed oxide scale at the oxide/alloy interface mediate protective behavior.
Lower cation diffusion rates and favorable interface energetics in Al- and Si-containing alloys promote slow growth of coherent mixed oxides.
The coherent mixed oxides produced in Al- and Si-containing alloys relieve thermal stress.
Relative to CrFeCoNi, Al-containing alloys will develop a more uniform, adherent, slowly growing, and persistent protective scale.
Relative to CrFeCoNi, Si-containing alloys will develop a more uniform, adherent, slowly growing, and persistent protective scale.
Relative to CrFeCoNi, Mn-containing alloys will develop a rapidly growing, inhomogeneous scale prone to cracking and spallation.
The CrFeCoNi baseline is expected to exhibit oxide-scale properties intermediate between the protective Al/Si variants and the degraded Mn variant.
The proposed comparison uses CrFeCoNi without X as the baseline control under otherwise identical exposure conditions.
The proposed exposure range is 900–1100 °C for tens to hundreds of hours in air or a controlled oxygen or corrosive atmosphere.
The hypothesis is intended to apply to well-characterized single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states at temperatures of at least 900 °C.
Similar oxide coherence, uniformity, and adhesion in the Mn, Al, and Si variants would falsify the predicted element-specific behavior.
A lack of significant diffusion or interfacial-energy differences correlated with scale properties would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis initially specifies exposure above 900 °C, whereas the intervention includes exactly 900 °C and the boundary uses ≥900 °C, leaving applicability at exactly 900 °C internally inconsistent.
